findings.title: deleteScheduledEmailReminder without referenceId deletes DB row but never cancels; immediate path never removes DB row
findings.body: When referenceId is null the function deletes the workflowReminder row and returns, which is fine. But when immediateDelete is true, the function sends the SendGrid cancel request and returns without deleting or updating the workflowReminder row, so a stale row stays in the DB with cancelled unset. The cron job's 'cancelled' sweep then never sees it and the row lingers until scheduledDate passes, and the reminder's referenceId stays unique-constrained against future use.

findings.title: Cancelled-but-not-immediate emails are only marked; the 'cancel' status set by cron is applied only within 1 hour of send
findings.body: Non-immediate deletion only sets cancelled=true. The cron (scheduleEmailReminders) only cancels reminders whose scheduledDate is within the next hour. Reminders cancelled earlier stay in SendGrid scheduled_sends and are sent later, which is the case the PR claims to fix; the window design should be justified, and any reminder whose booking is cancelled and whose scheduledDate is more than an hour out is still sent at its time if the cron's sweep is not reached before send. Also the row is never deleted if the cron's SendGrid call fails inside the try block, which aborts the whole loop.

findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders
findings.body: The loop calls client.request for each reminder inside a single try. If any request throws, the catch logs and the loop exits, so all subsequent cancelled reminders are not cancelled in SendGrid and their rows are not deleted, and the cron continues to send those emails. Each cancellation should be wrapped individually.

findings.title: Reminder rows deleted before the promise is awaited; Promise.all over unexecuted Prisma promises
findings.body: prisma.workflowReminder.delete returns a lazy PrismaPromise; it is only executed when awaited by Promise.all, which is outside the per-reminder loop. Any rejection (e.g. row already deleted by concurrent deleteMany) is caught only by the outer catch and aborts remaining work. Also the workflowRemindersToDelete type annotation is a Prisma__ client type that is unusual for this purpose.

findings.title: deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the DB row even when the Twilio cancel fails, and is now unconditional
findings.body: The new implementation calls twilio.cancelSMS inside the same try as prisma delete. If cancelSMS throws (e.g. message already sent or not found), the workflowReminder row is never deleted, and the caller in handleCancelBooking/bookings reschedule ignores the error. Conversely SMS reminders that were never scheduled (no referenceId) now still get a row delete that may fail for rows already removed. The SMS path also no longer supports the 'cancelled' deferral used for emails, so behavior is asymmetric.

findings.title: Reminder deletion is fire-and-forget; errors and DB writes are not awaited
findings.body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async but the forEach does not await them, and the earlier deleteMany of workflowReminder rows was removed. The cancel response is returned before the reminder updates complete, and any error is swallowed, so the booking cancellation can succeed while reminders are still scheduled.

findings.title: Rescheduled booking's reminders are cancelled with immediateDelete=true for email but not awaited
findings.body: The forEach calls the async deleteScheduledEmailReminder without awaiting, inside a try that cannot catch its rejections. Errors become unhandled promise rejections and the new booking flow proceeds before cancellation completes, so the old reminders may still be sent.

findings.title: Edited-step reminders deleted with forEach(async ...) and not awaited; scheduled rows still reference deleted data
findings.body: remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...) does not await the async delete calls, and the previous code's workflowReminder.deleteMany was removed, so rows for edited steps are now only marked cancelled or deleted asynchronously, racing with the subsequent scheduleEmailReminder calls that create new reminders for the same bookings.

findings.title: Broken JS in addedSteps / reformatted block: dayjs and BookingInfo not imported and PrismaPromise/Prisma value import
findings.body: The import list now imports PrismaPromise and Prisma as values from @prisma/client, and the commented-out testAction block was reformatted with broken indentation/comment nesting. The removed BookingInfo import is still referenced by `let evt: BookingInfo` in the commented region (fine), but `PrismaPromise` is used only as a type while imported as a value, and the trailing comma-less `Prisma` import is inconsistent with the rest of the file. Type-only imports should not be value imports.

findings.title: Changed signature of deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder breaks boolean-flag semantics
findings.body: The third parameter immediateDelete is passed as true in some callers and omitted in others with no documented contract; the meaning (cancel now vs. mark for cron) is implicit. Callers in workflows.tsx delete a deleted workflow's reminders immediately while bookings use deferred cancel, which is easy to get wrong and is not tested.

findings.title: No tests added for the new cancelled-flag cron path or the immediate/deferred branches
findings.body: The PR changes cancellation semantics across booking cancel, reschedule, workflow edit, and cron, yet adds no tests covering the cancelled flag, the 100-pending-cancellation failure mode, or the 1-hour cron window.
